title: Trunk-Based Development
description: Implement trunk-based development with short-lived branches, feature flags, and continuous integration.

data.text: Trunk-based development (TBD) is a source-control branching model where developers collaborate on a single branch called trunk (usually main or master). Short-lived feature branches, feature flags, and CI enable continuous integration without long-lived branches.

data.title: Trunk-based development rules
items: **Single long-lived trunk** — All developers commit to main (or merge short branches within a day)
**Short-lived branches** — Feature branches must be merged within hours, not weeks
**Feature flags** — Incomplete features are hidden behind flags, not hidden in branches
**CI on every commit** — The trunk must stay green; broken commits block everyone

data.title: Trunk-based with short-lived feature branches
data.code:
# Start a small feature branch from main
git switch -c feat/search-filters main

# Make small, focused commits
git commit -m "feat(search): add query parser"
git commit -m "feat(search): add filter UI component"

# Keep the branch short — merge same day
git switch main
git pull origin main
git merge --ff-only feat/search-filters

git push origin main

# Delete the branch immediately
git branch -d feat/search-filters

data.title: The 24-hour branch rule
data.text: A common trunk-based guideline is that feature branches must be merged within 24 hours. Longer branches defeat the purpose by creating merge conflicts and hiding integration problems.

Feature flags let you merge incomplete code to main without exposing it to users. The code is on main but the feature is disabled by default. This is the secret to TBD: trunk can always contain all code, but only flagged-on features are live.

items: **Boolean flags** in environment variables for simple on/off features
**Percentage rollouts** to gradually expose features to users
**Kill switches** to disable problematic features without a deploy
**Targeted flags** to show features to specific users or segments

data.text: Branch by abstraction is a technique for making large changes incrementally on main. You introduce an abstraction layer, migrate one caller at a time, then remove the old implementation — all on main without any long-lived feature branches.

data.title: Branch by abstraction: replacing a notification system
data.code:
Step 1: Introduce INotificationService abstraction
Step 2: Implement both OldEmailService and NewPushService
Step 3: Feature-flag which service is active (default: old)
Step 4: Merge to main with flag OFF
Step 5: Enable flag for internal users, verify
Step 6: Enable flag for all users
Step 7: Remove OldEmailService in a follow-up commit

All on main. No long-lived branch.

items: Run full test suite on every push to main
Block merges that would break the build
Use feature flags to keep incomplete features invisible in CI
Keep CI fast — slow CI slows down TBD significantly

items.question: Is trunk-based development the same as GitHub Flow?
items.answer: GitHub Flow is a form of trunk-based development. TBD is the broader model; GitHub Flow is one specific implementation of it.

items.question: How do I handle a feature that takes two weeks?
items.answer: Break it into smaller, independently shippable pieces. Each piece can be merged to main behind a feature flag. If you must have a long branch, reconsider whether trunk-based is right for this project.

items.question: What is the difference between trunk-based and mainline development?
items.answer: They are the same concept. 'Mainline' is the term from Perforce and SVN; 'trunk' is the Git-era term. Both describe a single integration branch that all developers merge to.

items.question: Does trunk-based require a CI/CD pipeline?
items.answer: Yes. Without fast, reliable CI, you cannot keep the trunk green. Investing in CI infrastructure is a prerequisite for TBD.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Trunk-based uses a single long-lived branch (main) for all integration
Feature branches must be short-lived — merge within 24 hours
Feature flags decouple deploy from release
Branch by abstraction enables large changes incrementally on main
Fast, reliable CI is a hard requirement for trunk-based development
